title: Circus during the war and the flu epidemic
summary: She toured with a circus during the First World War and caught the flu and pneumonia. She was told to stop singing for a year, and later went to Bucktown for fresh air.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Oh, well, 19, that time then. Yeah, that was before. That was after that. That was after that. Yeah. Because before that, I was with a circus during the time of the war. I was with a 35-car circus. Jones Brothers and Wilson Circus. Three-wing circus. I used to sing in a side show with the band. And I used to sing in the big show, in the concert with the band over there. And I used to ride in the street parade with the elephant. And that was during the flu epidemic when they closed all the shows in the theaters. Well, then that's where I caught the flu. I had the flu. And the doctor told me I should stop singing for at least a year. And I had signed up to go with the LG Barnes Circus in Venice, California. Well, after the doctor. Well, during my sickness, you know. He said that after I got so that he could tell me. He told me that twice they had walked out the room, thought I was dying. They said I had got double pneumonia. And he said that one of my lungs was affected. So I mustn't sing. I must not sing for at least a year. Well, I stopped singing for, I think, about a year and a half. Almost two years before I did any singing. And that's right after that is when I went to Bucktown. That's why Amos came by. He used to come and get me to take me to get fresh air. You know, tell me to go and get fresh air. And that's how he just asked me to come right out there to Bucktown. I was going out there to get fresh air.
